qualifying_findings.source_title: ReviewBench: An open benchmark for AI code review
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub announced ReviewBench, a research-preview benchmark for AI code review agents. The benchmark is built from 219 public pull requests across 19 languages, uses a multi-source golden set, labels findings by severity and category, and reports grounded and augmented precision and recall.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Code-review eval pages should distinguish known-finding recall from valid novel findings, preserve severity/category slices, and record the benchmark version, judge, matcher, and validation method before using a score as release evidence.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate destination: verification-and-evals. Treat ReviewBench as an evaluation-method example, not a local GitHub or Copilot product leaf.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare with existing AI code review and eval leaves, and avoid duplicating upstream product coverage.

qualifying_findings.source_title: New agent skill: Amazon SageMaker optimized generative AI inference for your coding agent
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: AWS introduced the aws-ai-ml skill through Agent Toolkit for AWS. The skill lets MCP-compatible coding agents such as Kiro, Claude Code, and Codex benchmark SageMaker endpoints, recommend deployment configurations, compare performance runs, and generate SageMaker Python SDK v3 code under the user's AWS credentials.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent-skill coverage should document credential scope, preflight confirmation for load tests, generated-code review, and the distinction between local skill installation and runtime discovery.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate destination: retrieval-and-tools or governance-and-risk. Keep only the practice lens: skill installation, discovery, benchmark authorization, generated-code review, and credential boundaries.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Check existing skill/tool-call practice pages before ingest; route AWS product details upstream.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Making Amazon Quick enterprise-ready: Automated, auditable cross-account resource promotion
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: AWS described a sample MCP server for promoting Amazon Quick agents, connectors, knowledge bases, flows, and spaces across accounts. The design uses idempotent upserts, read-only preview, permission replay, S3 backups before updates, and no deletes against the target.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent-resource promotion workflows should capture dry-run approval, idempotency, backup/rollback, no-delete posture, secret re-authentication, and permission replay as explicit release gates.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate destination: governance-and-risk and source-workflows. Treat the post as a promotion-control pattern for agent artifacts, not an Amazon Quick entity page.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, preserve the distinction between generated agent resources and source-code promotion.

qualifying_findings.source_title: IAM Enables AI Transformation at Oracle
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Oracle described IAM-centered controls for internal AI assistants and agents, including preserving employee permissions across MCP connections, denying destructive operations with service-specific policies, and preserving user/agent context across delegated MCP-compliant services.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: MCP governance pages should separate connector authentication from downstream authorization, document delegated identity propagation, and require explicit deny controls for destructive operations even when broader permissions exist.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate destination: governance-and-risk. Keep the downstream lens on delegated identity, least privilege, and action denial controls.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Avoid restating Oracle product background; compare with existing permissions and approvals pages.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Benchmarking MCP Servers and Stateful API Workflows: Latency, Throughput and Tokens per Call
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: API Coding argued that generic HTTP load tools do not measure MCP server cost well enough for agents. The post proposes per-tool latency percentiles, tools/list and discovery cost, JSON-RPC and isError error rates, payload sizes, and token-cost accounting for stateful workflows.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Tool evaluation pages should record context-cost and per-workflow measures, not only endpoint throughput. MCP benchmarking should treat tool definitions and results as recurring context costs.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate destination: retrieval-and-tools or verification-and-evals. Focus on measurement shape for governed tool use.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Potentially combine with MCP token-reducer item as one tool-cost practice leaf during ingest.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Most MCP Token Waste Is in Tool Results: Put a Deterministic Reducer Between Server and Model
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: API Coding proposed a deterministic reducer between MCP servers and models. The reducer would project, cap, strip, stash, and summarize tool results before the model sees them, while logging bytes, token estimates, and expansion references.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Context-architecture guidance should cover result-shaping, not only tool-schema search. Reducers need deterministic rules, visible truncation metadata, expansion paths, per-caller stashes, expirations, and accounting logs.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate destination: context-architecture and retrieval-and-tools. Capture the reducer as a local practice pattern for tool-result budgeting.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: If ingested, note that the proposed syntax is illustrative and not a shipped tool.

qualifying_findings.source_title: The Review Queue Is Your Real Agent Limit
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The post argues that agent rollout capacity should be modeled as risk-weighted review demand against effective reviewer-hours. It recommends measuring review-minutes rather than PR counts, tracking p50/p95 queue age by risk tier, using tiered review, and keeping independent verification separate from the authoring agent.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Team adoption guidance should treat human review as a capacity constraint. Agents should attach evidence, split oversized work, rebase stale changes, and repair failed checks rather than count as independent verification of their own output.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate destination: adoption-and-operating-model and agent-workflows. This is local practice coverage rather than ecosystem entity coverage.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare with existing review-capacity and agent PR pages.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Release-by-release analysis of AI coding agents
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: TurboAI describes release-by-release analysis for six AI coding agents, tracking environment variables, model IDs, default-model changes, flags, security hardening, billing corrections, official changelog links, and public documentation.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Coding-agent upgrade workflows should track environment variables, default model changes, hidden flags, security hardening, and billing corrections as release-risk inputs rather than relying on short changelog summaries.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate destination: governance-and-risk or coding-practices. Keep the release-diff method locally; route per-tool facts upstream.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Check whether an existing local page covers agent runtime upgrade checklists.

qualifying_findings.source_title: 5 Logging Habits That Make an AI Coding Agent Easier to Debug
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The guide recommends structured event fields, trace/span correlation, step sequencing, timing and outcome fields, and sensitive-data handling so failed AI coding-agent runs can be debugged from execution history rather than only final answers.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent workflow guidance should require observable event streams with tool, timing, status, trace context, and redaction fields when agents can call tools or delegate work.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate destination: agent-workflows or verification-and-evals. Focus on observability fields and debugging evidence.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Treat as secondary/practice source; verify with local observability pages before ingest.

qualifying_findings.source_title: MCP in Microsoft Foundry: The Toolbox Pattern for Trustworthy Tool Calling
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The guide explains Microsoft Foundry toolboxes as a centralized MCP-compatible endpoint and emphasizes that trustworthy tool calls still require separate agent and downstream identities, least-privilege tool exposure, namespaced tool names, and runtime approvals for human-authorized calls.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: MCP governance guidance should not equate central discovery with trust. It should document identity separation, allow-list filtering, approval points, and diagnostic naming for tool calls.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate destination: governance-and-risk and retrieval-and-tools. Keep only the trusted-tool-calling pattern locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: If ingested, verify against Microsoft Learn or another primary source before durable claims.
